mechanical.title: Mechanical design and analysis
mechanical.summary: Turn a performance need into a component or system that can be built and checked.
tasks: Translate the need into dimensions, loads and operating conditions.
Compare drawings or models and explain a design trade-off.
Work with manufacturing and test teams when a prototype behaves differently from the model.
mechanical.connection: A model is useful when its assumptions are clear and measurements can challenge it.

manufacturing.title: Manufacturing and quality work
manufacturing.summary: Make repeatable components and check that the output matches a specification.
tasks: Read a drawing or work instruction before setting up a task.
Measure key dimensions or properties and record the result.
Investigate variation rather than treating every difference as acceptable.
manufacturing.connection: Precision, tolerances and repeatable methods connect measurement to useful products.

instrument.title: Instrumentation and control
instrument.summary: Help a system turn physical conditions into dependable readings and actions.
tasks: Choose a measurement point and check the instrument's range.
Compare readings with a reference and investigate missing or unexpected values.
Use evidence to adjust a control or recommend a closer inspection.
instrument.connection: A reading depends on where and how it was measured, not just the number displayed.

support.title: Technical application support
support.summary: Help people use a technical product in the conditions of their own workplace.
tasks: Ask what the user is trying to measure or control.
Separate a setup problem from a sensor or process problem.
Explain the next diagnostic step and record what changed.
support.connection: Troubleshooting means testing explanations one at a time.

lab.title: Laboratory testing and analysis
lab.summary: Produce measurements that are useful because samples and comparisons are controlled.
tasks: Label and prepare samples so their identity stays traceable.
Change one planned factor while holding comparison conditions steady.
Report results with units, repeats and limitations.
lab.connection: Fair comparisons are more informative than an isolated result.

materials.title: Materials and formulation research
materials.summary: Investigate how a material's composition and structure relate to what it does.
tasks: Define a property that matters for the intended use.
Compare candidate materials using a stated method.
Explain trade-offs and what evidence is still missing.
materials.connection: A promising material must be evaluated against a specific task.

quality.title: Quality documentation and verification
quality.summary: Keep the chain from a test or batch to a decision clear enough to inspect.
tasks: Check which version of a method and sample was used.
Review whether measurements support the stated acceptance criteria.
Record a deviation and the evidence needed before releasing work.
quality.connection: A clear record makes a result checkable by someone who was not there.

data.title: Measurement software and data analysis
data.summary: Turn streams of measurements into displays and comparisons people can use.
tasks: Check timestamps, units and missing values.
Compare a new pattern with a defined baseline.
Test alerts against plausible alternative explanations.
data.connection: An alert is a reason to investigate, not proof of a single cause.

process.title: Process and systems engineering
process.summary: Connect material and energy changes to a sequence of equipment and operating choices.
tasks: Draw what enters and leaves each part of a process.
Compare equipment choices against the required conditions.
Use test results to revise the design and explain its limits.
process.connection: Conservation of matter and energy helps reveal missing assumptions.

logistics.title: Dispatch and logistics coordination
logistics.summary: Keep materials moving in the right order, with the information needed at each handoff.
tasks: Match deliveries or orders with available capacity.
Check timing, identification and handling requirements.
Respond to a delay without losing track of the product or customer need.
logistics.connection: A technically sound product can still fail its purpose if timing or handling goes wrong.

sonographer.title: Diagnostic medical sonographer
sonographer.summary: Acquire ultrasound images while supporting the person being examined.
tasks: Prepare for the requested examination and communicate with the patient.
Position the transducer and adjust acquisition settings to obtain useful views.
Document the images for interpretation within the clinical team's workflow.
sonographer.connection: Producing a clear measurement and interpreting its meaning are connected but different tasks.

radiologist.title: Radiologist
radiologist.summary: A physician who interprets medical images in clinical context.
tasks: Review images together with the clinical question.
Distinguish findings from uncertainty or imaging limitations.
Communicate an interpretation to the care team.
radiologist.connection: A picture is evidence to interpret, not a diagnosis by itself.

clinic.title: Medical office and booking support
clinic.summary: Help patients and clinical teams coordinate the information and appointments needed for care.
tasks: Handle appointment requests and confirm required information.
Communicate clearly with patients and modality teams.
Keep registration and scheduling records accurate.
clinic.connection: Care depends on reliable human coordination as well as instruments.

craft.title: Bootmaking and pattern work
craft.summary: Translate a design and material choice into a pair of boots through skilled craft.
tasks: Plan and cut pieces with attention to material stretch.
Join and shape components through stitching and lasting.
Inspect the finished result against the intended design and fit.
craft.connection: A flat pattern and a three-dimensional object have to agree.

acoustics.title: Acoustical consulting
acoustics.summary: Investigate how sound behaves in a space and recommend changes for its intended use.
tasks: Measure or model sound paths and levels.
Compare changes to room surfaces, layout or noise isolation.
Explain the trade-offs to the people designing or using the space.
acoustics.connection: Reflection and absorption become decisions about how a room works.

power.title: Power engineering and plant operations
power.summary: Operate and monitor equipment that produces or transfers thermal and electrical energy.
tasks: Read operating measurements and compare them with procedures.
Coordinate inspections and maintenance with other teams.
Track an abnormal condition and respond through established operating processes.
power.connection: Energy diagrams become real operating systems with constraints and losses.

refrigeration.title: Refrigeration and air-conditioning mechanic
refrigeration.summary: Install, maintain and troubleshoot equipment that moves heat and conditions air.
tasks: Use drawings to locate components and controls.
Check operating conditions and investigate a fault.
Repair or adjust equipment and verify the result.
refrigeration.connection: A refrigeration system moves heat; it does not create cold as a substance.

warehouse.title: Warehouse and inventory operations
warehouse.summary: Receive, locate and move goods while keeping identity and handling requirements visible.
tasks: Check incoming goods against shipment information.
Move and store products using appropriate equipment and procedures.
Maintain inventory records and coordinate outbound loads.
warehouse.connection: Temperature, time and correct identification all matter to a cold chain.
